scenes.title: tidydiversity
scenes.subtitle: Version 0.3.0 · coverage-based biodiversity in R: fair, fast, publication-ready
scenes.say: Meet Tidy Diversity version zero point three: biodiversity analysis in R that is fair, fast, and ready to publish.

scenes.title: Unequal sampling, unfair comparisons
bullets: Raw species counts measure sampling effort
Compare communities at equal sample coverage
Hill numbers: richness, Shannon, Simpson in one family
scenes.say: Sites are never sampled equally. Compare raw species counts, and you compare sampling effort, not nature. Tidy Diversity standardises by sample coverage, so every comparison is fair.

scenes.title: Tidy in, tidy out
scenes.say: One row per site and species goes in. A tidy table of Hill numbers comes out, for richness, Shannon and Simpson diversity, ready for d-plyr and g-g-plot.

scenes.title: Rarefaction and extrapolation by coverage
scenes.code:
curves <- div_rarefy(wet, q = c(0, 1, 2))
autoplot(curves, x = "coverage")
scenes.say: Rarefy and extrapolate to any sample coverage, and plot the curves in one line.

scenes.title: How much diversity is still unseen?
scenes.say: Asymptotic estimates, with bootstrap intervals, show how much diversity is still unseen in each season.

scenes.title: Taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity
scenes.code:
div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "PD", tree = tree)
div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "FD", distance = dist)
scenes.say: Taxonomic, phylogenetic and functional diversity share one framework, shown here for two Brazilian rainforest assemblages.

scenes.title: Fast where it matters
scenes.code:
system.time(iNEXT.3D::iNEXT3D(wide, diversity = "PD", PDtree = tree))
system.time(div_rarefy(brazil, abundance = n, type = "PD", tree = tree))
scenes.say: And it is fast. On the same data, phylogenetic rarefaction runs about {speedup_words} times faster than i-next 3 D, with identical results, thanks to compiled C plus plus kernels.

scenes.title: Beta diversity, turnover and nestedness
scenes.say: Beta diversity, turnover and nestedness come out as tidy tables and clear figures.

scenes.title: New: ask tidyvisor
scenes.code:
ord <- ord_fit(dune, method = "rda", formula = ~ Management + A1)
tidyvisor(ord)
scenes.say: New in this version: ask Tidy Visor. It explains your ordination in plain sentences, says when to follow up with pairwise PERMANOVA, and writes the results sentence for your paper.

scenes.title: Ready for the journal
bullets: Results sentences, tables and methods from tidyvisor
scenes.say: Every figure is sized for journal columns, with colour-blind-safe palettes, and the advice tells you what to report.

scenes.title: Full documentation online
scenes.say: Every function, tutorial and gallery example is on the package website, at tidy diversity dot in four metrix dot dev.

scenes.title: One family of packages
items: The statistical advisor for all three
scenes.say: Tidy Diversity works with Tidy Mapper and Tidy Epidemio, and Tidy Visor advises across all three.

scenes.title: Get started
scenes.say: Install Tidy Diversity from GitHub today, and find the full guide on the website.
